measures.what_it_does: Restores the Stevens County Rural Library District's (Libraries of Stevens County) regular property tax levy from $0.27 to $0.44 per $1,000 of assessed value for 2027 collection, to fund library operations, hours, staff and materials; that amount becomes the base for later limits (chapter 84.55 RCW). Colville and Kettle Falls are outside the district.
measures.cost_line: From $0.27 to $0.44 per $1,000 of assessed value for 2027 collection; about $51 a year ($4.25 a month) on a $300,000 home, per the statement for.
measures.pro_summary: The statement for (Sue Poe, Michelle Bauer, Joanie Matter) says the levy would let the library rehire staff and restore more than 100 open hours a week, including evenings and weekends; that residents borrowed $6.2 million of materials in 2025, four times what the library collects in taxes; and that libraries get no state or federal operating money.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed and no opposition committee was found. Voters rejected the same rate increase in April 2026, 53.85% to 46.15%.

taxes.basis: A yes vote is a levy lid lift that raises the library district's rate by about 63%, from $0.27 to $0.44 per $1,000, and resets the base for later years.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA voters' guide measure 7251 (S1); Spokesman-Review coverage of the April 2026 attempt (S2, S3); April 2026 results (S4); the 2014 precinct results showing Colville and Kettle Falls outside the district (S5); PDC committee record (S6).

measures.what_it_does: Sets Fire District 10's regular property tax levy at $0.75 per $1,000 of assessed value for 2027 collection, to keep operating and maintaining its fire vehicles, stations, trained personnel and equipment; that amount becomes the base for later limits (Resolution No. 2-2026).
measures.cost_line: $0.75 per $1,000 of assessed value for 2027 collection, up from the current $0.54: about $21 a year more per $100,000 of assessed value.
measures.pro_summary: No statement for was filed. The board's explanatory statement says the levy is needed to maintain current fire protection, suppression and emergency service and firefighter safety.
measures.con_summary: No statement against was filed and no opposition was found.

taxes.basis: A yes vote raises the district's levy rate by about 39%, from $0.54 to $0.75 per $1,000, and resets the base for later years: a levy lid lift.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA voters' guide measure 7323 (S1) is the only source found; no news coverage.

measures.what_it_does: Replaces the district's educational programs and operations levy, which expires in 2027, with a three-year levy (2028-2030) for staffing, safety, arts, nurses, counselors, class size, athletics, transportation and other costs the state does not fund (Resolution No. 11-26).
measures.pro_summary: No statement for was received by the deadline (committee: Supporting Nine Mile Students, Ann Fackenthall). Superintendent Jeff Baerwald says the levy is 17% of the budget; the district projects a lower combined school rate from 2028.
measures.con_summary: The statement against (NO Means NO! Voters Said NO Just 90 Days Ago!, David Joplin) says voters rejected a district levy 90 days earlier, that the levy lets the district spend on anything 'not funded by the State,' and that the district ranks 50th in income but 235th in dollars per student.

taxes.basis: A yes vote replaces an expiring EP&O levy at a lower estimated rate, $2.10 against the $2.27 collected in 2026; a replacement, not a new or larger tax.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA voters' guide measure 7330 (S1); Spokesman-Review coverage of the November levies (S2) and the failed April 2026 capital levy (S3); April 2026 Stevens results (S4).

measures.what_it_does: Authorizes a six-year capital levy (2027-2032) to replace a failing roof and condemned portable classrooms at Lakeside High School and modernize security, fire systems, facilities and infrastructure district-wide (Resolution No. 12-26).
measures.cost_line: Estimated $0.38 per $1,000 of assessed value: $774,853 in 2027 rising to $842,954 in 2032; the district says it matches the rate of a bond that expires January 1, 2027.
measures.pro_summary: The statement for (Future Focused For Nine Mile: Melanie Reynolds, Devin Bauer, Candace Haggard) says the levy keeps the current tax rate by replacing a bond that expires January 1, 2027, at the same 38 cents, and that the board cut projects after hearing tax concerns to fund a failed roof, condemned classrooms and fire and camera systems.
measures.con_summary: The statement against (NO Means NO! Voters Said NO Just 90 Days Ago!, David Joplin) says voters rejected a capital levy 90 days earlier, calls this version vague 'carte blanche' spending, says it recovers the district's election costs, and argues the condemned portables are not essential.

taxes.basis: Legally a new levy, but it continues the 38-cent rate of a construction bond that expires at the end of 2026, so a yes vote holds the district's rate in place; treated as a same-rate replacement.

measures.sources_note: VoteWA voters' guide measure 7331 (S1); Spokesman-Review coverage of the November levies (S2) and the failed April 2026 capital levy (S3); April 2026 Stevens results (S4).
